import re

lines = csv_content.strip().split('\n')
header = lines[0].split(',')
print(f"Columns: {header}")
print(f"Total data rows: {len(lines) - 1}\n")

# Find relevant column indices
header_lower = [h.strip().lower() for h in header]
print(f"Normalized headers: {header_lower}")

# Parse all rows and filter for James Okafor + Won status
won_deals_james = []
for line in lines[1:]:
    # Simple CSV parse (split by comma)
    fields = line.split(',')
    row = {header[i].strip(): fields[i].strip() for i in range(len(header))}
    
    # Check for James Okafor and Won status (case-insensitive)
    rep_col = [k for k in row if 'rep' in k.lower() or 'owner' in k.lower() or 'name' in k.lower() or 'sales' in k.lower()]
    status_col = [k for k in row if 'status' in k.lower() or 'stage' in k.lower() or 'result' in k.lower()]
    deal_col = [k for k in row if 'deal' in k.lower() or 'id' in k.lower()]
    
    # Try to match by checking all fields for "James Okafor" and "Won"
    row_str = line.lower()
    if 'james okafor' in row_str and 'won' in row_str:
        won_deals_james.append(row)

print(f"\nFound {len(won_deals_james)} won deals for James Okafor:\n")
for deal in won_deals_james:
    for k, v in deal.items():
        print(f"  {k}: {v}")
    print("---")

# Check for D001, D003, D006
deal_ids_found = []
for deal in won_deals_james:
    for v in deal.values():
        if re.match(r'D\d+', v):
            deal_ids_found.append(v)

expected = {'D001', 'D003', 'D006'}
found_set = set(deal_ids_found)

print(f"Found deal IDs: {found_set}")
print(f"All expected deals present: {expected.issubset(found_set)}")
